sourceAdaptationDecisions: Translate every learner-facing heading, gloss, example translation and source attribution; preserve every Japanese example/reading/form, type, tag, level and substantive comparison.
Retain all4declared source negative edges and3newprovider lessons. No optional navigation forces extra runtime objects;全然/あんまり are English-only explanatory evidence, never Russian placeholders.

Use the same truthful Russian title forじゃ/じゃあ/では/それでは. Exact-title deduplication already keeps those variants apart; no redundant six-edge clique is proposed. Full prose retains register, spelling, particles and discourse distinctions.

Renderあまり's negative beginner pattern naturally asнеочень/неособенно. State explicitly that negation comes from the predicate. Preserve quantity/frequency, surplus noun restricted toあまり and affirmative excess; do not infer polarity from the adverb alone.

Preserve conjunction versus noun coordination, additive versus temporal sequence, sequence versus cause and transition versus attached particles. Remove English-only tea-and-coffee/then/and comparisons but preserve each Japanese rule and original Japanese illustration.
Preserveだんだんdeveloping-change versus fixed slow speed and kango 段々 explanation;ちょうどphonetic 丁度 versus literal etymology;とてもnegative inability versus ordinary negative-degreeあまり.
Preserveまだ/もう polarity and stage distinctions plus remaining amount; preserve sourced bareもうsoon without a universal nonpast rule, and mixed-readingもう一度 classification.

Preserveよくfrequency/quality and adjectiveよ-forms;多分expectation rather than fixed odds;時々rendaku and all original frequency/weather examples. Make the source's rough frequency scale an explicit tendency, not a fixed mathematical interval or absolute boundary.

Preserve本当truth/genuineness andほんとvariant;現実actuality rather than necessarily disappointment;実際noun/practice/adverb distinctions and theory contrast. Keep mnemonics separate from historical etymology.
